newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy surprises analysts with FY97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy surprises analysts with FY97 profit.

text.p: Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co. Inc. said Wednesday its profits fell sharply in the latest quarter due to a tough retail environement.
But the earnings of $8.5 million, or 20 cents a share, for the fourth quarter in fiscal 1997, surprised analysts who had forecast a breakeven quarter.
Fourth quarter earnings were down from $19.8 million, or 46 cents a share, for the year-ago quarter.
"A challenging retail environment overshadowed our progress on several key initiatives to increase profitability," Best Buy Chief Executive Richard Schulze said in a statement.
Minneapolis-based Best Buy also reported a $1.7 million profit, or 4 cents per share, for the fiscal year 1997 ended March 1, vs. $48 million, or $1.10 per share, in the prior fiscal year..
The mean analyst forecast called for a break-even quarter and a loss of 14 cents a share for the year, according to First Call.

"As far as the quarter goes, it was definitely a surprise, so they got a nice positive number," John Hughes, analyst at Piper Jaffray Inc., said. "At the same time you need to put it in perspective... It was still a significant earnings decline" from the prior year.

Best Buy also warned that it expected to report a loss for the first half of fiscal 1998, as continued softness in a number of its categories and the company's decision to focus on more profitable product assortment should lead to declines in comporable-store sales, or sales at stores open at least a year.

However, improved earnings are expected for the fiscal year, Best Buy said, adding that it expects its gross profit margins will improve over last year due to growth in sales of service plans, better product assortment and more effective advertising and promotions.

Best Buy's inventories were down about $70 million at year end from a year ago. Also, interest expense in the fourth quarter was less than the comparable quarter of the prior year as lower inventories and reduced levels of recoverable costs from developed properties resulted in lower borrowings under the company's working capital credit facility.
Improved margins and inventory levels and less reliance on promotions were all seen as positive signs for Best Buy.
"It does indicate further evidence in the company's change in focus from growth as a primary corporate objective ... to profitability," Skip Helm, analyst at William Blair & Co. said.

But continued competition in the electronics market and the lack of hot new technologies to help drive sales are still problematic in the near-term for Best Buy and others in the industry, analysts said.
"I don't think a turnaround is completely in place" for Best Buy, Hughes said. "I think industry fundamentals are still challenging."
Best Buy stock rose $1.375 to close at $13.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
